answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity tied to verifiable compute. Before an agent can vote or earn, it must lock a refundable bond and prove it runs a genuine kernel of independently verified execution, not a free sign-up. Every extra identity then needs real computational work plus locked capital, so a sybil attacker cannot sprout endless cheap branches like a willow; each fake account costs as much as a real one, yielding no leverage from scattering influence across a knoll of puppet accounts. Peers can discount any identity whose stake or proven compute is too thin to be credible.
